'''Cory Allen Jefferson''' (born December 26, 1990) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Baylor University]] and represented the United States at the [[2013 Summer Universiade]] in [[Kazan, Russia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hill |first=Jerry |date=August 1, 2013 |title=WORLD TRAVELERS: International Experience Benefits Heslip, Jefferson |url=http://www.baylor.edu/bearfoundation/news.php?action=story&story=137894 |access-date=June 8, 2014 |website=Baylor.edu}}</ref>

==High school career==
Jefferson attended [[Killeen High School]] in [[Killeen, Texas]]. As a sophomore in 2006–07, he averaged 13.5 points, 10.5 rebounds and 5.1 blocks per game, earning All-District 16-4A first team honors. As a senior in 2008–09, he averaged 19.5 points and 6.2 rebounds per game, leading Killeen to three straight 30-win seasons and four consecutive district championship.<ref name="bio">{{Cite web |title=Corey Jefferson Bio |url=http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cory_jefferson_456100.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150326145221/http://www.baylorbears.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/cory_jefferson_456100.html |archive-date=March 26, 2015 |access-date=June 26, 2014 |website=BaylorBears.com}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Jefferson was listed as the No. 13 power forward and the No. 51 player in the nation in 2009.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Corey Jefferson recruiting profile |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Cory-Jefferson-66830;_ylt=AhW0MRstUjACswwNVjQKspFGPZB4 |access-date=September 16, 2015 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Cory Jefferson setting a pick (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Jefferson drawing a charge]]
In his freshman season at [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], Jefferson played sparingly for the Bears. In 21 games, he averaged 1.3 points and 1.2 rebounds in 4.6 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

After redshirting the 2010–11 season, Jefferson returned to the Bears for the 2011–12 season. In his sophomore season, he had 5 double-digit scoring and 12 multiple block games; his 42 blocks ranked 10th on Baylor's single-season list. In 34 games (one start), he averaged 3.6 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.2 blocks in 10.5 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

In his junior season, Jefferson was named to the NIT All-Tournament team after he helped Baylor win the NIT championship. He also earned Big 12 honorable mention honors at the end of the season. In 37 games (all starts), he averaged 13.3 points, 8.0 rebounds and 1.9 blocks in 27.9 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

In his senior season, Jefferson was named to the 2014 All-Big 12 third team. He was also named the 2014 USBWA District VII Player of the Year. In 38 games (all starts), he averaged 13.7 points, 8.2 rebounds and 1.3 blocks in 29.0 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==

===Brooklyn Nets (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Jefferson was selected with the final pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. He was later traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] on draft night.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 27, 2014 |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Draft Rights to Markel Brown, Xavier Thames and Cory Jefferson |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-draft-rights-markel-brown-xavier-thames-and-cory-jefferson |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140630065351/http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-acquire-draft-rights-markel-brown-xavier-thames-and-cory-jefferson |archive-date=June 30, 2014 |access-date=June 27, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He later joined the Nets for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 1, 2014 |title=Brooklyn Nets Announce Summer League Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster |access-date=July 1, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> and signed with the team on July 23.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 23, 2014 |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Markel Brown and Cory Jefferson |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-markel-brown-and-cory-jefferson |access-date=July 23, 2014 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Jefferson received his first and only start of the season on December 13 in a 114–87 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. In 23 minutes of action, he recorded 11 points on 5-of-5 shooting and 5 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 13, 2014 |title=Johnson leads hot-shooting Nets over Hornets |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141213/BKNCHA/gameinfo.html |access-date=October 15, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kharpertian |first=Devin |date=December 13, 2014 |title=Cory Jefferson, Moving Forward (HIGHLIGHTS) |url=http://thebrooklyngame.com/cory-jefferson-best-game-young-career/ |access-date=December 13, 2014 |website=TheBrooklynGame.com}}</ref> On January 1, 2015, using the flexible assignment rule, the Nets assigned Jefferson to the [[Maine Red Claws]], the affiliate of the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 1, 2015 |title=Nets assign Markel Brown and Cory Jefferson to D-League |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=17027 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150101195324/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=17027 |archive-date=January 1, 2015 |access-date=January 1, 2015 |website=InsideHoops.com}}</ref> On January 8, he was recalled by the Nets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 8, 2015 |title=Brooklyn Nets Recall Markel Brown and Cory Jefferson From NBA D-league |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-recall-markel-brown-and-cory-jefferson-nba-d-league |access-date=January 8, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On March 6, Jefferson recorded his first career double-double with season-highs of 12 points and 13 rebounds in over 15 minutes of action in a 108–100 overtime loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 6, 2015 |title=Suns rally late in 4th, beat Nets 108–100 in overtime |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150306/PHXBKN/gameinfo.html |access-date=October 15, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Buchanan |first=Zach |date=October 13, 2015 |title=Phoenix Suns' Cory Jefferson fighting for his spot |url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/10/12/phoenix-suns-cory-jefferson-fighting-roster-spot/73845124/ |access-date=October 13, 2015 |website=AZCentral.com}}</ref>

On June 29, 2015, Jefferson was named in the Nets' team for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=June 29, 2015 |title=BROOKLYN NETS ANNOUNCE SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER AND SCHEDULE |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster-and-schedule-2015 |access-date=June 29, 2015}}</ref> He managed three Summer League games for the Nets before being waived by the team on July 13.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 13, 2015 |title=BROOKLYN NETS REQUEST WAIVERS ON CORY JEFFERSON |work=NBA.com |url=http://www.nba.com/nets/brooklyn-nets-request-waivers-cory-jefferson |access-date=July 13, 2015}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2015–2016)===
On September 16, 2015, Jefferson signed a one-year, non-guaranteed contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 16, 2015 |title=Suns Sign Burton, Casey, Jefferson, Sims, White |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-burton-casey-jefferson-sims-white |access-date=September 16, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> After impressing head coach [[Jeff Hornacek]] and general manager [[Ryan McDonough (NBA executive)|Ryan McDonough]] during preseason, Jefferson made the Suns' opening night roster for the [[2015–16 Phoenix Suns season|2015–16 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |date=October 24, 2015 |title=Phoenix Suns keep Cory Jefferson, waive Henry Sims |url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/10/24/phoenix-suns-keep-cory-jefferson-waive-henry-sims/74537334/ |access-date=October 24, 2015 |website=AZcentral.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |date=October 24, 2015 |title=Cory Jefferson's effort earns Phoenix Suns roster spot |url=http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/10/24/cory-jeffersons-effort-earns-phoenix-suns-roster-spot/74561498/ |access-date=October 24, 2015 |website=AZcentral.com}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns on November 14, recording 2 points and 2 rebounds in a 105–81 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 14, 2015 |title=Bledsoe leads Suns over cold-shooting Nuggets, 105–81 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/DENPHX/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151116172902/http://www.nba.com/games/20151114/DENPHX/gameinfo.html |archive-date=November 16, 2015 |access-date=November 14, 2015 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On January 7, 2016, he was waived by the Suns after appearing in just six games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 7, 2016 |title=Suns Waive Cory Jefferson and Bryce Cotton |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-waive-cory-jefferson-and-bryce-cotton |access-date=January 7, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref>

On January 20, 2016, Jefferson was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns|Bakersfield Jam]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 20, 2016 |title=JAM ACQUIRE CORY JEFFERSON |url=http://bakersfield.dleague.nba.com/news/jam-acquire-cory-jefferson/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160127003859/http://bakersfield.dleague.nba.com/news/jam-acquire-cory-jefferson/ |archive-date=January 27, 2016 |access-date=January 20, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> The next day, he returned to the Suns, signing a 10-day contract with the team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 21, 2016 |title=Suns Sign Cory Jefferson |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-cory-jefferson |access-date=January 21, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> After his 10-day contract expired, playing two more games with the team in the process, he was not retained by the Suns.

===Bakersfield Jam (2016)===
On February 1, 2016, Jefferson was reacquired by the Bakersfield Jam.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA D-League Transactions |url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160203061520/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=February 3, 2016 |access-date=February 2, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.}}</ref> The next day, he made his debut for the Jam in a 132–111 win over the [[Oklahoma City Blue]], recording 18 points, 14 rebounds, 3 assists and 1 block in 34 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2, 2016 |title=White Pours In 37 As Jam Cruise By Blue |url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160202/OKLBAK/ |access-date=February 2, 2016 |website=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc. |archive-date=February 6, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160206170020/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20160202/OKLBAK/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2016–2017)===
In July 2016, Jefferson joined the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.fearthesword.com/2016/7/12/12160146/cavs-summer-league-grades-after-first-three-games Cleveland Cavaliers Summer League Grades After First Three Games]</ref> On September 26, 2016, he signed with the Cavaliers,<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 26, 2016 |title=Cavaliers Announce 2016–17 Training Camp Roster |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/training-camp-roster-2016-17 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160926191342/http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/training-camp-roster-2016-17 |archive-date=September 26, 2016 |access-date=September 26, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> but was later waived on October 20 after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 20, 2016 |title=Cavaliers Waive Three Players |url=http://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/waive-three-players-161020 |access-date=October 20, 2016 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He ultimately joined the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]] on November 12, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miller |first=Meagan |date=November 12, 2016 |title=Austin Spurs Acquire Cory Jefferson |url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-cory-jefferson/ |access-date=November 13, 2016 |website=NBA.com |archive-date=November 14, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161114173057/http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-cory-jefferson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On February 6, 2017, he was named in the Western Conference All-Star team for the 2017 NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2017 |title=Rosters for 2017 NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire |url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/ |url-status=dead |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Philippines (2017)===
In March 2017, he signed with the [[Alaska Aces (PBA)|Alaska Aces]] as the team's import for the [[2017 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sacamos |first=Karlo |title=Alaska finds Octavius Ellis replacement in nick of time with ex-Nets forward Cory Jefferson |url=http://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/news/alaska-commisioners-cup-import-cory-jefferson-octavius-ellis-replacement |access-date=March 16, 2017 |publisher=spin.ph |publication-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref>

===Olimpia Milano (2017–2018)===
On July 16, 2017, Jefferson signed with the [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 16, 2017 |title=Cory Jefferson signs with Olimpia Milano |work=Sportando.com |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/241356/cory-jefferson-signs-with-olimpia-milano.html |access-date=August 8, 2017}}</ref> On February 2, 2018, he parted ways with Milano.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 2, 2018 |title=Olimpia Milano, Cory Jefferson part ways |work=Sportando.com |url=https://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/263436/olimpia-milano-cory-jefferson-part-ways.html |access-date=February 2, 2018}}</ref>

===Texas Legends (2018)===
On February 22, 2018, the [[Texas Legends]] had acquired Jefferson from [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] with Clipper's 2018 NBA G League draft 4th round pick and the returning player right to [[Cameron Ayers]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 22, 2018 |title=Legends Acquire Cory Jefferson in Trade With Clippers |work=NBA.com |url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-cory-jefferson-trade-clippers/ |access-date=February 22, 2018}}</ref>

===Darüşşafaka (2018)===
On July 13, 2018, Jefferson signed with the Turkish team [[Darüşşafaka S.K.|Darüşşafaka]] of the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 13, 2018 |title=Darussafaka tabs Jefferson for frontline |work=EuroLeague.net |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8vdw9ysqrwbknt5e/darussafaka-tabs-jefferson-for-frontline |access-date=July 13, 2018}}</ref> However, on August 18, 2018, Darüşşafaka parted ways with Jefferson after he did not pass the physical test.<ref>{{Cite news |date=August 18, 2018 |title=Cory Jefferson, Darussafaka part ways |work=Sportando.basketball |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turkey/bsl/285937/cory-jefferson-darussafaka-part-ways.html |access-date=August 18, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2018–2019)===
Jefferson was signed by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on October 12, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 12, 2018 |title=Team Signs Jefferson, Johnson |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/team-signs-jefferson-johnson |access-date=October 12, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He was waived the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 13, 2018 |title=76ers cuts include veteran center Emeka Okafor |url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/10/13/76ers-release-emeka-okafor |access-date=October 14, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Jefferson was added to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] training camp roster.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 22, 2018 |title=Blue Coats Announce Training Camp Roster and Schedule |url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-announce-training-camp-roster-and-schedule/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181027232036/https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-announce-training-camp-roster-and-schedule/ |archive-date=October 27, 2018 |access-date=October 27, 2018 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

===Guangzhou Long-Lions (2019)===
On January 16, 2019, Jefferson signed with [[Guangzhou Long-Lions]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carchia |first=Emiliano |date=January 16, 2019 |title=Guangzhou Lions officially sign Cory Jefferson |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/guangzhou-lions-officially-sign-cory-jefferson |access-date=January 16, 2019 |newspaper=Sportando |archive-date=February 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205201032/https://sportando.basketball/en/guangzhou-lions-officially-sign-cory-jefferson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Jefferson made his debut for the Long-Lions on the same day, scoring 17 points with six rebounds and a block in a 133–92 win over the [[Beikong Fly Dragons]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 16, 2019 |title=Regular Season Round 32: Beijing Dragons – Guangzhou LL 92–133 |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/boxScores/China/2019/0116_15106_3514.asp |access-date=January 16, 2019 |website=eurobasket.com}}</ref> On February 11, 2019, Jefferson parted-way with the Long-Lions after his import player roster spot was replaced by [[Lorenzo Brown]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 12, 2019 |title=CBA官方：广州男篮签约洛伦佐-布朗替代科里-杰弗森 |url=https://voice.hupu.com/cba/2393722.html |access-date=February 12, 2019 |website=hupu.com |language=zh}}</ref>

===Gran Canaria (2019)===
On February 22, 2019, [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]] of the [[Liga ACB]] announced the signing of Jefferson.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 22, 2019 |title=EL HERBALIFE GRAN CANARIA INCORPORA A CORY JEFFERSON |url=https://cbgrancanaria.net/news/el-herbalife-gran-canaria-incorpora-a-cory-jefferson/ |access-date=February 22, 2019 |website=cbgrancanaria.net |language=ES}}</ref> He and Gran Canaria parted away just after six games, on April 9, 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 8, 2019 |title=Cory Jefferson, Gran Canaria part ways |language=en-US |publisher=Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cory-jefferson-gran-canaria-part-ways/ |access-date=April 9, 2019 |archive-date=February 5, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230205201022/https://sportando.basketball/en/cory-jefferson-gran-canaria-part-ways/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Atléticos de San Germán (2020)===
On February 22, 2020, Jefferson signed with [[Atléticos de San Germán]] of the Puerto Rican league.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 22, 2020 |title=Cory Jefferson joins Atléticos de San Germán |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/cory-jefferson-joins-atleticos-de-san-german/ |access-date=February 22, 2020 |website=Sportando|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

On May 27, 2021, Jefferson tried out for the Big3 tryouts in Dallas and made the final 5 for a finalist spot in Las Vegas.
